requirements.requirement: Add at least 512MB compressed in-memory swap on node1
requirements.summary: zram-generator installed and /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf configured a 1024MB (>512MB) zstd-compressed zram0 device; systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service created the device and swapon --show/proc/swaps confirmed a 1024M zram0 swap entry, well above the 512MB minimum.
swapon --show and /proc/swaps show /dev/zram0 (1024M) active immediately after configuration, and zramctl confirms zstd compression algorithm and non-zero total/compressed size.

requirements.requirement: zram swap active at boot (persists across restart)
requirements.summary: dev-zram0.swap is WantedBy=swap.target via the generator drop-in, so it activates automatically every boot without manual enablement. This was directly verified through a full reboot: pre-restart boot_id 7223d5b7... and healthy zram swap baseline captured, systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect, node unreachable across several poll attempts (expected disruption), then reachable again with a new boot_id 63e7fef2... and low uptime (4.7s), after which swapon --show/proc/swaps/zramctl confirmed /dev/zram0 (1024M, zstd, priority 100) active again as [SWAP]. This is a complete pre-restart baseline, disruption, and recovery transition.

requirements.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: swap-priority=100 was set for zram0, verified via swapon --show showing zram0 at priority 100 versus the pre-existing disk swap /dev/vda3 at priority -2, both before and after the reboot — the kernel prefers higher-priority swap devices, so zram is used first.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task: it installed zram-generator and configured a 1024MB zstd-compressed zram0 swap device with swap-priority=100 (well above disk swap's -2), confirmed it active immediately, and proved boot persistence with a genuine end-to-end restart test (pre-reboot baseline, reboot acknowledgement, observed disconnection, new boot_id, and post-reboot confirmation that zram0 is again active and prioritized above disk swap). This restart evidence also satisfies the independent provider-wide node-restart protocol for the sole managed node. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were introduced; hygiene is very clean aside from a trivial leftover log file.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; long-term stability across multiple reboots or under memory pressure was not tested, though this is beyond what the task requires.

The compression ratio/effectiveness of zstd was not exercised under real memory load (zramctl showed near-empty usage), so functional compression benefit under load is inferred from configuration rather than directly measured.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: package install (cmd-5968f6f267dd44a7), writing the zram-generator config (cmd-aef3d8480f37488c), starting the generated setup/swap units (cmd-ab8e11075fd6470a, cmd-5ecf7abfdd1242a6), and the reboot used to gather the required boot-persistence evidence (cmd-f0b300bd1a64479f). No unrelated or experimental mutations were found; discovery/status commands (cmd-b9900e6b19d9421a, cmd-6814a1f3551c4a24, cmd-b80afdaaf9ea45a6) and reboot polling commands were read-only. The four failed/errored commands are expected: cmd-b9900e6b19d9421a returned 1 only because zram-generator wasn't yet installed at that discovery point, and the three connection-timeout/reset polls during the reboot window reflect the expected disruption, not unwanted state changes. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small log file created by the backgrounded reboot command and left in place — negligible, bounded, and a natural byproduct of the required restart-evidence step rather than an unnecessary mutation. Lifecycle diffs (listening-socket PID churn, systemd-private tmp dirs) are normal reboot artifacts, not executor-caused residue.
